To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
pressure ulcers occur in 36.5 and 39.5% of patients with SCI during acute and functional rehabilitation, respectively.

the occurrence of pressure sores in patients with spinal-cord injury is 39%, that pressure sores are more likely to develop when patients are incontinent, have pneumonia, and when their motor function is less complete, and that pressure sores that develop during acute rehabilitation are a strong predictor of pressure sores developing during rehabilitation.

the occurrence of pressure ulcer is high in patients with SCI during in-patient rehabilitation and that a history of pressure ulcer during acute in-patient rehabilitation is a strong predictor for pressure ulcer development during functional rehabilitation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a group of patients with SCI with a high risk of developing a pressure ulcer.
pressure ulcer incidence in the acute phase of spinal cord injury.
the occurrence and predictors of pressure ulcer during primary in-patien rehabilitation of SCI patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of a pressure ulcer at the start of rehabilitation increases the likelihood of a pressure ulcer occurring during rehabilitation.
pressure ulcer prevention should start as soon as possible after the onset of the SCI and that the prevention should be maintained throughout the rehabilitation phase and beyond.
pressure ulcer prevention should be a high priority in SCI rehabilitation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the occurrence of pressure ulcer during functional rehabilitation is high and that the risk of pressure ulcers is increased in case of having a pressure ulcer at admission, motor completeness of the injury, tetraplegic lesion and/or pneumonia and/or pulmonary diseases.
pressure ulcers in SCI patients during primary in-patent rehabilitation are common and are associated with several risk factors.

the occurrence and risk factors for pressure ulcer development during functional rehabilitation are comparable to other studies and that having had a pressure ulcers during acute rehabilitation phase is the strongest predictor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pressure ulcer occurrence during acute rehabilitation is a significant predictor for pressure ulcers occurring during functional rehabilitation.
the occurrence of pressure ulcer during acute and functional rehabilitation is high.
prevention should start at admission and continue during rehabilitation.
